# useContractorList

<a id="usecontractorlist"></a>

> **useContractorList**(`input`: [`UseContractorListProps`](#usecontractorlistprops)): [`UseContractorListResult`](#usecontractorlistresult)

Fetches a paginated list of a company's contractors and decorates each entry with the actions
allowed for its current onboarding/employment state.

## Remarks

`contractorType` maps to a server-side filter and changes which actions appear on each row:
`'active'` exposes `view` plus `dismiss`/`cancel_dismissal`/`cancel_rehire`, `'terminated'`
exposes `view` plus `rehire`/`cancel_dismissal`/`cancel_rehire`, `'onboarding'` and the
unfiltered default expose `edit`/`cancel_self_onboarding`/`delete`. Omit `contractorType` to
list every contractor. `'active'` and `'terminated'` are complementary server-side filters, so
every onboarded contractor appears under exactly one of them — including one whose scheduled
rehire has yet to take effect, who stays under `'terminated'` until their start date.

Page changes use placeholder data: the previous page stays rendered while the next one loads,
and `status.isFetching` flips to `true` during the request.

Sorting is applied by the API, so the order holds across pages. No sort is requested until
`sort.onSortChange` is called, leaving the list in the API's default order until then, and
calling it with `undefined` returns the list to that default order. Applying or clearing a sort
returns to page 1 because the API sorts before it paginates. The sort persists across
`contractorType` changes, since every filter sorts by the same field.

The endpoint rejects a sort combined with a search term (HTTP 422), so a search filter added
here would have to clear the sort.

## Example

```tsx title="Example"
import { useContractorList } from '@gusto/embedded-react-sdk'

function ActiveContractors({ companyId }: { companyId: string }) {
  const contractorList = useContractorList({ companyId, contractorType: 'active' })

  if (contractorList.isLoading) return <div>Loading...</div>

  return (
    <ul>
      {contractorList.data.contractors.map(contractor => (
        <li key={contractor.uuid}>
          {contractor.businessName ?? [contractor.firstName, contractor.lastName].join(' ')}
          {contractor.allowedActions.includes('cancel_dismissal') && (
            <button onClick={() => contractorList.actions.onCancelDismissal(contractor.uuid)}>
              Cancel dismissal
            </button>
          )}
        </li>
      ))}
    </ul>
  )
}
```

### ContractorAction

> **ContractorAction** = `"edit"` \| `"delete"` \| `"cancel_self_onboarding"` \| `"view"` \| `"dismiss"` \| `"rehire"` \| `"cancel_dismissal"` \| `"cancel_rehire"`

<a id="contractorsortfield"></a>

### ContractorSortField

> **ContractorSortField** = `"name"`

Field the contractor list can be sorted by.

#### Remarks

`'name'` sorts by last name for individual contractors and by business name for business
contractors, matching how each row is labelled.
